question: An administrator says 'no' to your staffing proposal because it costs too much. What is your best next move?

options.A: Organize a violent protest outside the administrative office
options.B: Prepare constructive evidence showing long-term cost savings and safety
options.C: Threaten the administrator with a media boycott
options.D: Abandon the advocacy campaign immediately and give up

explanation: Smart thinking! Coming back with solid proof that your idea improves safety and saves money in the long run is way more effective than getting upset. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of family planning counselling?

options.A: Ensuring every client chooses modern barrier methods
options.B: Reducing the overall birth rate in rural communities
options.C: Convincing every client to use permanent surgical methods
options.D: Helping clients make free and informed reproductive choices

explanation: Counselling empowers clients to make voluntary decisions about their own families rather than forcing a specific choice upon them. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: What is a major long-term health complication frequently managed by nurses in patients who have undergone child marriage and early pregnancy?

options.A: Accelerated bone mineralization and high density

options.C: Obstetric fistula and severe pelvic floor damage
options.D: Chronic respiratory infections from cold weather

question: What key visual finding does a clinician look for on the cervix during a speculum exam for acute cervicitis?

question: A patient with Pick's disease tries to wander out of the ward wearing only a hospital gown. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Apply soft wrist restraints immediately to prevent wandering attempts.
options.B: Gently redirect the patient toward a quiet lounge area with a familiar activity.
options.C: Explain firmly and logically why leaving the ward is dangerous for health.
options.D: Lock the patient inside the hospital room until visiting hours are over.

explanation: Redirection is your best friend here! Arguing or reasoning usually fails because of brain damage, but gently steering them to a cozy spot keeps them safe without a fight. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h6)

question: What does the abbreviation LMP stand for in nursing assessments?

options.A: Last menstrual period
options.B: Luteal menstrual phase
options.C: Low mucosal pressure
options.D: Latest medical procedure

question: Where in the body would you look for multi-unit smooth muscle?

options.A: In the walls of the urinary bladder
options.B: In the iris of the eye controlling the pupil
options.C: In the muscular walls of the stomach
options.D: In the middle layer of the small intestine

explanation: Multi-unit muscle gives us fine, precise control—just like adjusting your camera lens or how your iris changes the pupil size in bright light! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why should nursing leaders join daily safety huddles during a culture change?

options.A: It prevents doctors from questioning the clinical decisions made by nurses

options.C: It ensures that nurses finish their morning documentation much faster
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further written incident reporting

explanation: Exactly! When leaders 'walk the talk' and show up for frontline safety routines, it builds real trust with the nursing team. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why do we count water as a nutrient even though it gives us zero calories?

options.A: It breaks down into simple sugars inside the stomach lining
options.B: It is essential for life, acting as a medium for all metabolic reactions
options.C: It stimulates the production of digestive enzymes in the pancreas
options.D: It converts directly into structural tissue during growth phases

explanation: Correct! A nutrient is anything needed for survival and body chemistry—it doesn't have to provide energy to be vital. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h4)

question: What is the main reason hospitals try to build a 'blame-free' reporting culture?

options.A: To encourage staff to report errors and near misses honestly
options.B: To make sure negligent workers never face legal consequences
options.C: To hide hospital mistakes from government regulators
options.D: To reduce the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily

explanation: When staff aren't terrified of punishment, they speak up about close calls and mistakes. That honesty is how we fix things and protect future patients! [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary benefit of a spinal reflex bypassing the brain?

options.A: It stops sensory signals from reaching the skin
options.B: It allows a person to consciously choose how to respond
options.C: It stores long-term memories of painful events
options.D: It allows for much faster reaction times to protect the body

explanation: By bypassing conscious processing in the brain, spinal reflexes can trigger an immediate motor response to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h1)

question: What should a nurse do immediately if the physical count of pethidine does not match the register balance?

options.A: Add personal money to replace any missing tablets
options.B: Wait until the next shift to see if the count balances out
options.C: Report the discrepancy right away to the nursing supervisor
options.D: Cross out the wrong number and write a new one quietly

explanation: Missing drugs could indicate theft or error, requiring immediate official investigation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h7)

question: A family member asks how to help a relative overcome a bad driving phobia. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Do all the driving for them so they never feel anxious again
options.B: Insist they drive on busy highways immediately to get over it
options.C: Hide all car keys so they forget about driving completely
options.D: Encourage small steps of progress and avoid enabling total avoidance

question: What are small pieces of digital data called when they travel across a network?

options.A: Pixels
options.B: Packets

question: What do we call the deep worry families feel about potentially losing a loved one with HIV?

options.A: Chronic denial syndrome
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Situational psychosis
options.D: Secondary infection

explanation: Well done! Anticipatory grief happens when families start grieving and worrying about future loss long before any severe physical decline occurs. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h2)

question: Which injection site is generally considered the safest for adult patients?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Dorsogluteal
options.C: Ventrogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

question: What do biochemical tests mainly measure to help identify an unknown bacterium?

options.A: The patient's immune antibody response to the infection
options.B: The exact physical length and width of the cell wall
options.C: The specific chemical and metabolic activities of the organism
options.D: The genetic sequence of the organism's outer capsule

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring devices in nursing informatics?

options.A: To completely replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.B: To automatically track patient physiological status in real time
options.C: To manually calculate monthly hospital billing statements
options.D: To serve as a decorative fixture at the hospital bedside

question: An LTC nurse spends a big part of the shift supervising nursing assistants. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To minimize direct nurse interaction with residents
options.B: To ensure delegated tasks are performed safely and correctly
options.C: To complete administrative paperwork required by the hospital
options.D: To replace the need for formal care planning meetings

question: What is the vault of the baby's skull made of?

options.C: Unfused compressible bones

question: What is the primary function of a Primary Care Provider (PCP) in an HMO system?

options.A: Manufacturing generic drugs for local pharmacies
options.B: Acting as the first point of contact and medical gatekeeper
options.C: Performing complex open-heart surgeries daily
options.D: Auditing the financial books of the HMO company

question: How does vitamin C help your body when you eat it along with beans?

options.A: It increases the absorption of plant-based iron
options.B: It prevents the protein in beans from causing gas
options.C: It turns the complex carbohydrates into simple sugars
options.D: It slows down digestion so you feel full longer

question: A community health center needs funds to buy routine vaccines. Which funding source should they look to?

options.A: The Basic Health Care Provision Fund
options.B: International research grants for cancer treatment

question: When we talk about 'social capital' in a community, what do we mean?

options.A: The trust and supportive networks built through social participation
options.B: The physical infrastructure of roads and water pipes
options.C: The total financial savings kept in local credit unions
options.D: The government grants given to public health clinics

question: As a community health nurse collaborating with a new NGO team, what should you focus on first?

options.A: Working in complete isolation to protect professional authority
options.B: Building collaborative teamwork and respecting local cultural values
options.C: Insisting that all traditional birth attendants stop practicing
options.D: Refusing to share patient health records with anyone

question: What actually makes air rush into your lungs when you take an inhalation?

question: What is a major duty of a Community Health Officer (CHO) at a primary health center?

options.B: Auditing national health ministry financial records

question: Which of the following is one of the famous 'five rights' of clinical delegation?

options.A: Right ward location

question: What is capitation in the context of HMO operations?

question: What is the primary way an HMO is funded by its members?

options.A: Paying a fixed periodic fee in advance

options.C: Paying the hospital cash after every treatment
options.D: Paying the government a monthly tax

question: Which tiny projections form the brush border right on the surface of intestinal cells?

question: Why does a peri-operative nurse need both strong clinical skills and great communication?

question: Which ethical principle guides a nurse's duty to act in the best interest of their psychiatric patient?

question: Why do wards track specific numbers like infection rates?

question: How do unit managers usually help with hospital budgeting?

question: What do we call an evaluation check that looks at whether a community can keep up health benefits after funding ends?

options.A: Effectiveness
options.B: Sustainability
options.C: Efficiency

question: What is the primary purpose of inserting an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To secure and maintain a patent airway

question: What is a key requirement for valid informed consent regarding medication administration?

options.A: The doctor orders the drug without explaining side effects

question: Why do nurses sometimes hesitate to ask patients about their spiritual needs?

options.A: Lack of available paperwork charts in the nursing station

options.C: Fear of imposing personal values or causing offense

question: Where should a nurse document a medication error and the subsequent patient assessment?

question: Where should you place the measuring tape to get an accurate head circumference on a newborn?

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) in the ward?

question: How does cigarette smoking increase the risk of developing vulval tumours?

options.C: It impairs local immunity and works with HPV to promote cell changes

question: You find a weeping trader sitting alone after a market fire. What is your best first move using PFA?

options.C: Refer the trader directly to a psychiatric hospital for formal psychotherapy
options.D: Administer a strong oral sedative to prevent immediate panic attacks

question: What is the primary physiological problem in all forms of distributive shock?

question: A patient tells you they plan to stop their blood pressure medication as soon as they feel better. What should you as a nurse do?

question: What happens to the foetal skull bones during the process of molding?

options.C: They expand outward to make the head rounder

question: What is the main job of the vascular tunic?

question: What is the main job of our gastrointestinal (GI) tract?

question: What is the main difference between crowd management and crowd control?

question: Why do we keep our fingers pointing upward or straight down toward the sink drain when rinsing our hands?

question: Which of these actions goes against safe infection control practice during venepuncture?

question: A community health nurse is planning outreach for an area with high youth unemployment. What is the main challenge fresh school leavers usually face?

question: What is the rule regarding breast milk that has been frozen and then thawed for a feeding?

question: Why do large hospitals rely heavily on computer servers?

question: A patient is admitted with a ruptured appendix and severe abdominal rigidity. Which type of emergency is this?

question: Why is educating the girl child considered so important for Primary Health Care?

question: A nurse in a primary health clinic assesses a child with severe dehydration and lethargy. What is the most appropriate immediate clinical action?

question: A patient has a long-standing infection that cuts down blood supply, making the affected cells shrink. What is this adaptation called?

question: When assessing female sexual health, why is it important to look beyond just physical health?

question: What is the most immediate danger when someone has severe, nonstop vomiting and diarrhea?

question: Which of these is a key clinical sign or indicator that a QA committee tracks?

question: Why is protecting patient privacy so important during a chart review for a study?

question: What is a common clinical pitfall when dealing with a patient showing signs of maladaptation?

question: A ward manager checks how often nurses wash their hands before doing wound dressings. What kind of indicator is this?

question: What is the most common minor issue that can happen after a paracentesis?

question: What is the main reason a hospital reviews things after an adverse event happens?

question: Why do public health teams collect blood or stool samples during a suspected outbreak?

question: Why are home visits by community health workers so helpful for new mothers?

question: Why must you stabilize a patient thoroughly before loading them into a transport vehicle?

question: What tool do Nigerian nurses commonly use in local clinics to track a child's growth and immunization records?

question: How should a nurse respond when a community attributes an illness to traditional or spiritual causes?

question: If an intracardiac needle is placed too far to the side (laterally), which major organ might accidentally get punctured?

question: What is the standard prescription cream applied from the neck down to treat scabies?

question: What causes the sudden symptoms of Katayama fever (acute schistosomiasis)?

question: What is osteomyelitis?

question: What is the biggest factor in whether a GPI patient will fully get their memory and thinking back after treatment?

question: A patient with terminal cancer feels too tired to finish three standard meals a day. What is the best nursing action?

question: How do computers directly help keep patients safe during medication rounds?

question: What is the body's main use for carbohydrates?

question: Why are local disaster teams so important when an emergency strikes?

question: Which of these is a major environmental sign of high health risk in a community?

question: What is the primary goal of an IEC program in primary health care?

question: Why is community participation essential for the long-term success of public health interventions?

options.C: Share the details on a personal social media account without privacy filters
options.D: Call every single staff member individually during their busy morning rounds

explanation: Group messaging allows charge nurses to efficiently broadcast general updates and policy changes to an entire team at once. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h2)

question: What does the term 'food security' refer to in nutritional nursing assessments?

options.A: Having reliable access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food
options.B: Eating only foods that have been certified organic by government agencies
options.C: Keeping hospital kitchen supplies locked away from pests
options.D: Storing perishable groceries at the correct refrigerator temperature

explanation: Food security means an individual has physical and economic access to the food they need for an active, healthy life. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h5)

question: What should you tell a patient who says they need their rescue SABA inhaler multiple times every day?

options.A: Stop taking the rescue inhaler immediately and switch to drinking warm water
options.B: Contact your healthcare provider because increased use suggests worsening disease control
options.C: Double your daily dose of long-acting medication to make up for the breakthrough symptoms
options.D: This is a normal expected outcome of long-term therapy that requires no action

explanation: If a rescue inhaler is needed constantly, it's a sign that the underlying condition isn't well controlled. The doctor needs to review and adjust their daily management plan. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which alternative exit route for drugs is especially important for nurses to remember when caring for breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: Mammary excretion
options.B: Sweat gland secretion
options.C: Salivary elimination
options.D: Pulmonary excretion

explanation: Drugs can pass into breast milk through the mammary glands. As nurses, we always check if a mother's medications are safe for her breastfeeding infant! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h5)

question: When is it appropriate to begin the secondary survey on an emergency patient?

options.A: At the exact moment the ambulance arrives at the gate
options.B: Only after the patient is transferred to the main ward
options.C: After life-threatening primary survey issues are managed
options.D: Before the patient even enters the triage waiting area

explanation: The secondary survey is delayed until the ABCDE primary survey is completed and the patient is stable. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on authority figures for your clinical decisions?

options.A: Institutional leaders have no clinical background
options.B: Authority figures are impossible to locate in a hospital
options.C: Senior nurses refuse to speak with junior staff
options.D: Experts may base views on custom rather than evidence

explanation: Even experienced experts can fall back on outdated habits if their views aren't backed by solid, current research. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h3)

question: How do tummy cramps from gut spasms usually feel?

options.A: As sharp, crampy abdominal pain
options.B: As a dull, constant burning in the chest
options.C: As sudden weakness and muscle stiffness
options.D: As painless swelling in the lower belly

explanation: When gut muscles squeeze way too hard, it results in uncomfortable, sharp cramping in the tummy. You'll often see patients clutching their bellies because of this! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h1)

question: When a client wants to switch to a different birth control method during a follow-up visit, what is your main job as a nurse?

options.A: Charge an extra administrative fee for changing the care plan
options.B: Refuse service until a senior medical officer approves the change
options.C: Force the client to continue the original method for at least one more year
options.D: Ensure there is no gap in contraceptive coverage to prevent unintended pregnancy

explanation: When changing methods, timing is everything. We must make sure there is no unprotected gap where an unintended pregnancy could happen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)
